headline: AI Company Valued at $1.25 Trillion Announces Plan to One Day Discover What a Profit Is
subheadline: Fresh from raising $15 billion, the frontier lab unveiled its long-term roadmap: AGI by whenever, revenue by eventually, and an actual business model 'under active research'.
author: Dexter Appiah-Clarke, Markets & Meaning Desk
seoTitle: AI Firm Valued at $1.25 Trillion Still Researching Profits | The Daily Absurd
seoDescription: Satire: an AI company raised $15 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation and is reportedly getting close to working out what money is for.
sourceEvent: OpenAI reportedly raised $15 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation in November 2026 — roughly half its original target — amid quarterly revenue of about $10 billion.

social.x: An AI company just raised $15bn at a $1.25 trillion valuation and says it's close to understanding what 'profit' means. The valuation is not satire. The rest is. Barely.
social.facebook: You know your industry is normal when a company worth more than most countries describes profitability as an open research problem.
altHeadlines: Investors Value Company at $1.25 Trillion; Company Values Investors' Optimism
AI Lab Promises Profits Right After It Finishes Counting the Money

body:
A leading artificial intelligence company has raised $15 billion at a valuation of $1.25 trillion, money it reportedly plans to invest in the industry's most elusive research target to date: figuring out how a business works.

The raise — described by insiders as 'only' half the original target, the way one describes a mountain as 'only' twice the size of another mountain — cements the company's position as the most valuable organisation ever to use the phrase 'path to profitability' without a map.

"People ask when we'll be profitable," said a fictional senior strategist, adjusting a lanyard that cost more than a house. "That's the wrong frame. We're a research organisation. The research question is: what if money went in a circle?"

Economists note the valuation is based on rigorous financial methodology, including the time-tested metrics of 'vibes', 'the other guy got it', and 'imagine if it works'. With quarterly revenue reportedly around $10 billion, the company's price-to-actual-things ratio has entered territory previously explored only by tulips and enthusiasm.

The firm insists the economics make sense once you account for future revenue from enterprises, consumers, governments, and — in the advanced models — concepts not yet invented.

Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve's latest stability report found that 87% of market contacts now cite AI as a top risk, with the remaining 13% believed to work in AI.

At press time, the company had announced its next funding round would be open to anyone, on the principle that a valuation this size can only be sustained if it becomes a group activity.
